author: Henry Adams
plan_notes: Lean deterministic plan: per-chapter targets apportioned by source-word share; extradiegetic chapters excluded. No prepass, no signature enumeration.

segments.classification_reason: Author's own preface establishing narrative voice
segments.title: PREFACE

signatures.passage_hint: What could become of such a child of the seventeenth and eighteenth centuries, when he should wake up to find himself required to play the game of the twentieth?
signatures.why: Founding question of the whole book; introduces the card-game metaphor.

signatures.passage_hint: As it happened, he never got to the point of playing the game at all; he lost himself in the study of it, watching the errors of the players; but this is the only interest in the story, which otherwise has no moral and little incident.
signatures.why: Authorial statement of the book's method and its self-irony; completes the game metaphor.

signatures.passage_hint: Of all this that was being done to complicate his education, he knew only the color of yellow.
signatures.why: Signature ironic contrast between world-historical change and the infant's sense impression.

signatures.passage_hint: Summer was the multiplicity of nature; winter was school.
signatures.why: Aphorism that seeds the unity/multiplicity theme of the closing chapters.

signatures.passage_hint: the man who pretended they were not, was in his eyes a schoolmaster--that is, a man employed to tell lies to little boys.
signatures.why: Characteristic barb about teachers, which later turns ironic when he becomes one.

signatures.passage_hint: Above all, he had held his tongue.
signatures.why: First instance of the silence motif that recurs to the final chapter.

signatures.passage_hint: no one suggested at that time a doubt whether a system of society which had lasted since Adam would outlast one Adams more.
signatures.why: Adam/Adams wordplay; the child's unquestioned continuity.

signatures.passage_hint: Sixty years afterwards he was still unable to make up his mind. Each course had its advantages, but the material advantages, looking back, seemed to lie wholly in State Street.
signatures.why: Chapter's closing cadence of undecided retrospect.

signatures.passage_hint: even when only ten years old, his face was already fixed, and his heart was stone, against State Street; his education was warped beyond recovery in the direction of Puritan politics.
signatures.why: States the inherited bias as a fixed warp.

signatures.passage_hint: Charles Francis Adams possessed the only perfectly balanced mind that ever existed in the name.
signatures.why: Central judgment of the father, later tested in London.

signatures.passage_hint: The world never loved perfect poise. What the world does love is commonly absence of poise, for it has to be amused.
signatures.why: Aphoristic explanation of why the father was called cold.

signatures.passage_hint: Sumner was the boy's ideal of greatness; the highest product of nature and art.
signatures.why: Fixes the hero-worship that later breaks.

signatures.passage_hint: All experience since the creation of man, all divine revelation or human science, conspired to deceive and betray a twelve-year-old boy who took for granted that his ideas, which were alone respectable, would be alone respected.
signatures.why: Signature ironic hyperbole about a misleading education.

signatures.passage_hint: Boston had solved the universe; or had offered and realized the best solution yet tried. The problem was worked out.
signatures.why: Ironic summary of Unitarian complacency.

signatures.passage_hint: He thought his mind a good enough machine, if it were given time to act, but it acted wrong if hurried. Schoolmasters never gave time.
signatures.why: Mind-as-machine self-analysis; grievance against school.

signatures.passage_hint: the facile use of only four tools: Mathematics, French, German, and Spanish.
signatures.why: The four tools are a recurring measure of his deficiency.

signatures.passage_hint: he wondered whether their education on Boston Common had taught Savage and Marvin how to die.
signatures.why: Retrospective, chilling payoff of the snowball fight.

signatures.passage_hint: like white Greek temples in the abandoned gravel-pits of a deserted Syrian city.
signatures.why: Distinctive image of unfinished Washington.

signatures.passage_hint: Even at twelve years old he could see his own nature no more clearly than he would at twelve hundred, if by accident he should happen to live so long.
signatures.why: Characteristic self-irony on self-knowledge.

signatures.passage_hint: Slavery was wicked, and slavery was the cause of this road's badness which amounted to social crime--and yet, at the end of the road and product of the crime stood Mount Vernon and George Washington.
signatures.why: The chapter's central contradiction.

signatures.passage_hint: the faculty of ignoring them makes the practical man; but any attempt to deal with them seriously as education is fatal.
signatures.why: Aphorism on contradiction and practicality.

signatures.passage_hint: he learned the nature of a flagrantly corrupt political bargain in which he was too good to take part, but not too good to take profit.
signatures.why: Epigram of the first practical political lesson.

signatures.passage_hint: As a politician, he was already corrupt, and he never could see how any practical politician could be less corrupt than himself.
signatures.why: Self-indictment that carries the moral confusion forward.

signatures.passage_hint: Speaking as an American of 1900, he had as yet no education at all. He knew not even where or how to begin.
signatures.why: Closing formula of the chapter.

signatures.passage_hint: Four years of Harvard College, if successful, resulted in an autobiographical blank, a mind on which only a water-mark had been stamped.
signatures.why: Core image of the college's effect.

signatures.passage_hint: It taught little, and that little ill, but it left the mind open, free from bias, ignorant of facts, but docile.
signatures.why: Balanced backhanded verdict.

signatures.passage_hint: yet to stand alone is quite natural when one has no passions; still easier when one has no pains.
signatures.why: Aphoristic deflation of the class's independence.

signatures.passage_hint: Strictly, the Southerner had no mind; he had temperament.
signatures.why: Blunt typological judgment, later qualified by Adams's own likeness to Lee.

signatures.passage_hint: he needed to read mathematics, like any other universal language, and he never reached the alphabet.
signatures.why: Mathematics failure, a recurring deficiency.

signatures.passage_hint: remained always an insect, or something much lower--a man.
signatures.why: Ironic reversal on Concord transcendentalism.

signatures.passage_hint: like so many mirrors of himself, an infinite reflection of his own shortcomings.
signatures.why: Climactic image of the classmates as judges.

signatures.passage_hint: As yet he knew nothing. Education had not begun.
signatures.why: Closing formula.

signatures.passage_hint: A FOURTH child has the strength of his weakness.
signatures.why: Aphoristic opening that sets the chapter's ironic self-valuation.

signatures.passage_hint: He liked it best when he hated it. Education began at the end, or perhaps would end at the beginning.
signatures.why: Signature paradox and chiasmus about retrospective education.

signatures.passage_hint: His first lecture was his last.
signatures.why: Compressed reversal that carries the Berlin university failure.

signatures.passage_hint: All State education is a sort of dynamo machine for polarizing the popular mind
signatures.why: Early dynamo image that the late chapters' force theory builds on.

signatures.passage_hint: came from time wasted; studies neglected; vices indulged; education reversed;--it came from the despised beer-garden and music-hall; and it was accidental, unintended, unforeseen.
signatures.why: Founding statement of 'accidental education', a key recurring concept.

signatures.passage_hint: A prison-wall that barred his senses on one great side of life, suddenly fell, of its own accord, without so much as his knowing when it happened.
signatures.why: Central image of the Beethoven awakening.

signatures.passage_hint: it should not be again in Berlin.
signatures.why: Closing resolution and cadence.

signatures.passage_hint: Education founded on mere self-interest was merely Guelph and Ghibelline over again--Machiavelli translated into American.
signatures.why: Concludes the moral dilemma about violent political concentrations.

signatures.passage_hint: no woman had ever driven him wrong; no man had ever driven him right.
signatures.why: Lifelong 'law' about women; recurs thematically.

signatures.passage_hint: "Sir, I am a tourist!"
signatures.why: Comic self-verdict on eighteen months.

signatures.passage_hint: Rome was the worst spot on earth to teach nineteenth-century youth what to do with a twentieth-century world.
signatures.why: Thesis of Rome as seductive anti-education.

signatures.passage_hint: Rome was actual; it was England; it was going to be America.
signatures.why: Key leap linking Roman failure to American destiny.

signatures.passage_hint: who went on repeating to himself the eternal question:--Why! Why!! Why!!!--as his neighbor, the blind beggar, might do
signatures.why: Typographic escalation and the beggar image at Ara Coeli.

signatures.passage_hint: Substitute the word America for the word Rome, and the question became personal.
signatures.why: Personalizes the historical question.

signatures.passage_hint: The lesson of Garibaldi, as education, seemed to teach the extreme complexity of extreme simplicity; but one could have learned this from a glow-worm.
signatures.why: Recurring formula, deflated by the glow-worm.

signatures.passage_hint: to begin the study of law and to vote for Abraham Lincoln on the same day.
signatures.why: Ironic hinge opening the chapter.

signatures.passage_hint: tossed into space by an unknown energy which played with all his generation as a cat plays with mice.
signatures.why: Force imagery and generational helplessness.

signatures.passage_hint: from whom one could learn nothing but bad temper, bad manners, poker, and treason.
signatures.why: Bathetic catalogue on the cotton planters.

signatures.passage_hint: a young mosquito--a private secretary--trying to buzz admiration in the ears of each
signatures.why: Self-belittling image between Sumner and Seward.

signatures.passage_hint: "If there's no secession now, you and I are ruined."
signatures.why: Seward's attributed dialogue; tactical candor.

signatures.passage_hint: a long, awkward figure; a plain, ploughed face; a mind, absent in part, and in part evidently worried by white kid gloves
signatures.why: Lincoln portrait whose misjudgment is the point.

signatures.passage_hint: the rule that a friend in power is a friend lost.
signatures.why: Founding maxim repeated in later chapters.

signatures.passage_hint: This time the pitcher of education had gone to the fountain once too often
signatures.why: Proverb adapted to the education refrain.

signatures.passage_hint: with much the same outfit as Admiral Dupont would have enjoyed if the Government had sent him to attack Port Royal with one cabin-boy in a rowboat.
signatures.why: Sets up the recurring cabin-boy image.

signatures.passage_hint: He never labored so hard to learn a language as he did to hold his tongue, and it affected him for life.
signatures.why: Origin of the lifelong reticence and silence theme.

signatures.passage_hint: a family of early Christian martyrs about to be flung into an arena of lions, under the glad eyes of Tiberius Palmerston.
signatures.why: Signature comic-grand image.

signatures.passage_hint: not a word escaped; not a nerve twitched.
signatures.why: The father's poise under the shock.

signatures.passage_hint: Empires were always tumbling to pieces and diplomats were always picking them up.
signatures.why: Aphorism of diplomatic indifference.

signatures.passage_hint: At intervals during the next thirty years Henry Adams continued to happen upon the Duke, who, singularly enough, was always playing leap-frog.
signatures.why: Deadpan comic payoff.

signatures.passage_hint: He was mistaken--of course!
signatures.why: Self-corrective reversal.

signatures.passage_hint: young Adams neither hated nor wanted to kill his friends the rebels, while he wanted nothing so much as to wipe England off the earth.
signatures.why: Sets out the chapter's foes/friends inversion in the young man's rage.

signatures.passage_hint: Self-restraint among friends required much more effort than keeping a quiet face before enemies.
signatures.why: The aphoristic core of the chapter's title.

signatures.passage_hint: for if Mr. Lincoln was not what they said he--was what were they?
signatures.why: The punchline of the Thackeray episode, with its exact dash rhythm.

signatures.passage_hint: and was finally announced as "Mr. Halexander Hadams," and under this name made his bow for the last time to Lord Palmerston who certainly knew no better.
signatures.why: Comic climax of the footman sequence; it needs the Handrew/Hanthony setup before it.

signatures.passage_hint: It was a laugh of 1810 and the Congress of Vienna.
signatures.why: Characterizes Palmerston as an anachronism.

signatures.passage_hint: Then he said curtly: "Palmerston wants a quarrel!"
signatures.why: The Minister's terse speech at the crisis.

signatures.passage_hint: He's a cross between the devil and the Duke of Argyll!
signatures.why: Stirling's verdict on Swinburne, which Adams then glosses.

signatures.passage_hint: One who could feel neither Hugo nor Landor was lost.
signatures.why: Swinburne's test and Adams's self-condemnation.

signatures.passage_hint: "Then, Mr. Weed, do you think that no politician can be trusted?" Mr. Weed hesitated for a moment; then said in his mild manner: "I never advise a young man to begin by thinking so."
signatures.why: The central exchange that frames the chapter's question of trust.

signatures.passage_hint: "The world can absorb only doses of truth," he said; "too much would kill it."
signatures.why: Evarts's counter-maxim, paired with Weed's.

signatures.passage_hint: In truth, the Legation knew, then, all that was to be known, and the true fault of education was to suspect too much.
signatures.why: The ironic turn after Granville's letter.

signatures.passage_hint: "I asked him if I was to understand that policy as not now to be changed; he said: Yes!"
signatures.why: Russell's categorical assurance, which Napoleon's later 'No!' exposes.

signatures.passage_hint: One's diplomatic education was a long mistake.
signatures.why: The retrospective verdict.

signatures.passage_hint: The only resolute, vehement, conscientious champion of Russell, Napoleon, and Jefferson Davis was Gladstone.
signatures.why: Punchline of the reversed valuations.

signatures.passage_hint: he was obliged at last to admit himself in error, and to consent in spirit--for by that time he was nearly as dead as any of them--to beg his pardon.
signatures.why: The self-mortifying conclusion on Palmerston.

signatures.passage_hint: only a mistake, but one of incredible grossness
signatures.why: Gladstone's own phrase, which Adams turns back on him here and in the next chapter.

signatures.passage_hint: His son, a nervous animal, made life a terror by seeing too much.
signatures.why: Contrasts the son's temperament with the father's.

signatures.passage_hint: They were learning from the Yankees how to fight.
signatures.why: Ironic close of the July 1863 climax.

signatures.passage_hint: with a whoop of triumph he rushed to throw both arms about his neck and kiss him on both cheeks.
signatures.why: Milnes's embrace before Delane.

signatures.passage_hint: "You come next!" would have been the friendly warning.
signatures.why: Unspoken retort to Delane.

signatures.passage_hint: It would be superfluous in me to point out to your lordship that this is war!
signatures.why: The Minister's famous sentence.

signatures.passage_hint: The war was Russell's war--Adams only accepted it.
signatures.why: The secretary's reading of the note.

signatures.passage_hint: as the final result of combined practice, experience, and theory--he proved it.
signatures.why: Ironic collapse of his theory.

signatures.passage_hint: Earl Russell was certainly not one of the two.
signatures.why: Closing one-line deflation, which needs Gladstone's 'one or two' setup.

signatures.passage_hint: Henry Adams was Darwinist because it was easier than not, for his ignorance exceeded belief
signatures.why: Self-deprecating thesis.

signatures.passage_hint: it was the very best substitute for religion; a safe, conservative, practical, thoroughly Common-Law deity.
signatures.why: Uniformity as a secular religion.

signatures.passage_hint: One had been, from the first, dragged hither and thither like a French poodle on a string, following always the strongest pull
signatures.why: An image of passivity before force that anticipates the dynamic theory.

signatures.passage_hint: the first vertebrate was a very respectable fish
signatures.why: Comic setup for Pteraspis.

signatures.passage_hint: One's instinct abhors time.
signatures.why: The Wenlock meditation's core.

signatures.passage_hint: he could prove only Evolution that did not evolve; Uniformity that was not uniform; and Selection that did not select.
signatures.why: Key paradox, recalled in Twilight.

signatures.passage_hint: what he valued most was Motion, and that what attracted his mind was Change.
signatures.why: Seeds the later philosophy.

signatures.passage_hint: He was a Darwinian for fun.
signatures.why: Punchline of the confession.

signatures.passage_hint: he had become an estray; a flotsam or jetsam of wreckage; a belated reveller, or a scholar-gipsy like Matthew Arnold's. His world was dead.
signatures.why: Signature self-portrait of the survivor from the fifties.

signatures.passage_hint: the more he knew, the less he was educated.
signatures.why: Core paradox of the book's education motif.

signatures.passage_hint: The generation between 1865 and 1895 was already mortgaged to the railways, and no one knew it better than the generation itself.
signatures.why: Thesis about the railway era that recurs in later chapters.

signatures.passage_hint: He was for sale, in the open market.
signatures.why: Blunt market idiom for the young man's position.

signatures.passage_hint: At thirty years old, the man who has not yet got further than to study the situation, is lost, or near it.
signatures.why: Aphoristic self-judgment.

signatures.passage_hint: Mr. Seward came and had his whist, and Adams remembered his rough parting speech: "A very sensible entertainment!"
signatures.why: Seward's only voiced line and the closure of that relation.

signatures.passage_hint: Sumner's mind had reached the calm of water which receives and reflects images without absorbing them; it contained nothing but itself.
signatures.why: Distinctive psychological image of Sumner.

signatures.passage_hint: he had to admit that nine-tenths of his acquired education was useless, and the other tenth harmful.
signatures.why: Chapter's summary verdict on his education.

signatures.passage_hint: The tourist was the great conservative who hated novelty and adored dirt.
signatures.why: Epigram on his rococo mood.

signatures.passage_hint: He had never seen Nature--only her surface--the sugar-coating that she shows to youth.
signatures.why: Opens the 'last lesson'.

signatures.passage_hint: Nature enjoyed it, played with it, the horror added to her charm, she liked the torture, and smothered her victim with caresses.
signatures.why: Central image of sensuous, cruel Nature.

signatures.passage_hint: For pure blasphemy, it made pure atheism a comfort. God might be, as the Church said, a Substance, but He could not be a Person.
signatures.why: Theological conclusion; exact wording matters.

signatures.passage_hint: Mont Blanc for a moment looked to him what it was--a chaos of anarchic and purposeless forces
signatures.why: First vision of chaos, which anticipates the late theory.

signatures.passage_hint: Patriotism seemed to have been brought out of the Government stores, and distributed by grammes per capita.
signatures.why: Satire of the Paris war.

signatures.passage_hint: but the honors of piracy resemble the colors of the begonia; they are showy but not useful.
signatures.why: Begonia motif that pays off later.

signatures.passage_hint: "If you will point out to me any one who knows more, Mr. Adams, I will appoint him."
signatures.why: Eliot's line; must be paired with Adams's preceding protest.

signatures.passage_hint: A parent gives life, but as parent, gives no more. A murderer takes life, but his deed stops there. A teacher affects eternity; he can never tell where his influence stops.
signatures.why: Famous triadic aphorism.

signatures.passage_hint: In essence incoherent and immoral, history had either to be taught as such--or falsified.
signatures.why: Teaching dilemma in exact form.

signatures.passage_hint: nine minds in ten take polish passively, like a hard surface; only the tenth sensibly reacts.
signatures.why: Premise for the method of cultivating the tenth mind.

signatures.passage_hint: "The degree of Harvard College is worth money to me in Chicago."
signatures.why: Student's answer that upsets his experience.

signatures.passage_hint: to make a social desert that would have starved a polar bear.
signatures.why: Image of Cambridge society.

signatures.passage_hint: Friends are born in archaic horizons; they were shaped with the Pteraspis in Siluria; they have nothing to do with the accident of space.
signatures.why: Friendship meets the Pteraspis motif.

signatures.passage_hint: One friend in a lifetime is much; two are many; three are hardly possible.
signatures.why: Aphorism that prepares the later trio of King, Hay and Adams.

signatures.passage_hint: Education, systematic or accidental, had done its worst. Henceforth, he went on, submissive.
signatures.why: End of the first half of the book.

signatures.passage_hint: What one knows is, in youth, of little moment; they know enough who know how to learn.
signatures.why: Restated purpose of the book.

signatures.passage_hint: Education had ended in 1871; life was complete in 1890; the rest mattered so little!
signatures.why: Marks the twenty-year gap without narrating it.

signatures.passage_hint: He went home as a horse goes back to his stable, because he knew nowhere else to go.
signatures.why: Image of resigned return.

signatures.passage_hint: As the Niagara was to the Teutonic--as 1860 was to 1890--so the Teutonic and 1890 must be to the next term--and then?
signatures.why: First acceleration calculation, which anticipates the later law.

signatures.passage_hint: as though playing a garden hose on a thirsty and faded begonia.
signatures.why: Pays off the begonia motif.

signatures.passage_hint: Like the others, the priest saw only what he brought. Like all great artists, St. Gaudens held up the mirror and no more.
signatures.why: Mirror principle for the Rock Creek figure.

signatures.passage_hint: At past fifty, Adams solemnly and painfully learned to ride the bicycle.
signatures.why: Comic deflation.

signatures.passage_hint: Even dead men allow themselves a few narrow prejudices.
signatures.why: Closing irony that sets up distrust of bankers.

signatures.passage_hint: the sudden appearance of Germany as the grizzly terror which, in twenty years effected what Adamses had tried for two hundred in vain--frightened England into America's arms--seemed as melodramatic as any plot of Napoleon the Great.
signatures.why: Ironic family-historical frame for the Anglo-American rapprochement.

signatures.passage_hint: Never before had Adams been able to discern the working of law in history, which was the reason of his failure in teaching it, for chaos cannot be taught
signatures.why: Key statement linking the lifelong search for law to his failure as a teacher.

signatures.passage_hint: After all, friends had done the work, if not one's self, and he too serves a certain purpose who only stands and cheers.
signatures.why: Self-mocking spectator stance.

signatures.passage_hint: In his fancy, office was poison; it killed--body and soul--physically and socially.
signatures.why: Recurring 'power is poison' doctrine.

signatures.passage_hint: his poison was that of the will--the distortion of sight--the warping of mind--the degradation of tissue--the coarsening of taste--the narrowing of sympathy to the emotions of a caged rat.
signatures.why: Characteristic accumulating dashes; defines the poison precisely.

signatures.passage_hint: his obedience to the President's order was the gloomiest acquiescence he had ever smiled.
signatures.why: Compressed paradox of Hay's character.

signatures.passage_hint: Adams, you reason too much!
signatures.why: La Farge's standing reproach; a hinge between Bostonian reason and artistic nuance.

signatures.passage_hint: Practical politics consists in ignoring facts, but education and politics are two different and often contradictory things.
signatures.why: Aphorism stating the chapter's tension between politics and education.

signatures.passage_hint: Before the end, one began to pray to it; inherited instinct taught the natural expression of man before silent and infinite force.
signatures.why: Central image of the dynamo as religious object.

signatures.passage_hint: his historical neck broken by the sudden irruption of forces totally new.
signatures.why: Comic-catastrophic climax of the search for sequence.

signatures.passage_hint: he would risk translating rays into faith.
signatures.why: Statement of method: measuring force by its attraction on the mind.

signatures.passage_hint: she was the animated dynamo; she was reproduction--the greatest and most mysterious of all energies; all she needed was to be fecund.
signatures.why: Equates goddess and dynamo.

signatures.passage_hint: An American Virgin would never dare command; an American Venus would never dare exist.
signatures.why: Antithetical aphorism on American sexlessness.

signatures.passage_hint: I darted a contemptuous look on the stately monuments of superstition.
signatures.why: Gibbon's phrase, on which the Amiens episode turns.

signatures.passage_hint: To Adams she became more than ever a channel of force; to St. Gaudens she remained as before a channel of taste.
signatures.why: Resolution of the Adams and St. Gaudens contrast.

signatures.passage_hint: All the steam in the world could not, like the Virgin, build Chartres.
signatures.why: Chapter's definitive aphorism.

signatures.passage_hint: The value of a Ming vase was more serious than universal war.
signatures.why: Ironic summation of relative values.

signatures.passage_hint: History broke in halves.
signatures.why: Terse verdict on Hay's China stroke.

signatures.passage_hint: Life is so gay and horrid!
signatures.why: Hay's refrain, repeated in p7.

signatures.passage_hint: the affectation of readiness for death is a stage role, and stoicism is a stupid resource, though the only one. Non doles, Paete! One is ashamed of it even in the acting.
signatures.why: Oblique grief at King's departure.

signatures.passage_hint: as though thirty years were a shadow, and he were again to fall into King's arms at the door of the last and only log cabin left in life.
signatures.why: Payoff of the Estes Park meeting.

signatures.passage_hint: as though he were still Adam in the Garden of Eden between God who was unity, and Satan who was complexity, with no means of deciding which was truth.
signatures.why: Central unity/complexity figure.

signatures.passage_hint: For human purposes a point must always be soon reached where larger synthesis is suicide.
signatures.why: Key aphorism on 'larger synthesis'.

signatures.passage_hint: A seeker of truth--or illusion--would be none the less restless, though a shark!
signatures.why: Characteristic deflating close.

signatures.passage_hint: His single thought was to keep in front of the movement, and, if necessary, lead it to chaos, but never fall behind. Only the young have time to linger in the rear.
signatures.why: Elderly resolve with an ironic twist.

signatures.passage_hint: Flattery had lost its charm, but the Fluch-motif went home.
signatures.why: Closing aphorism on Wagner and catastrophe.

signatures.passage_hint: Adams proclaimed that in the last synthesis, order and anarchy were one, but that the unity was chaos.
signatures.why: Core doctrine of the conservative Christian anarchist.

signatures.passage_hint: Russia became luminous like the salt of radium; but with a negative luminosity as though she were a substance whose energies had been sucked out--an inert residuum--with movement of pure inertia.
signatures.why: Signature image of Russian inertia.

signatures.passage_hint: For him, all opinion founded on fact must be error, because the facts can never be complete, and their relations must be always infinite.
signatures.why: Epistemic refusal.

signatures.passage_hint: and there the newer Teufelsdrockh sat dumb with surprise, and glared at the permanent electric lights of Hammerfest.
signatures.why: Title image.

signatures.passage_hint: The electro-dynamo-social universe worked better than the sun.
signatures.why: Wry verdict on hearing of McKinley within the Arctic night.

signatures.passage_hint: one great empire was ruled by one great emperor--Coal.
signatures.why: Chapter's conclusion.

signatures.passage_hint: Roosevelt, more than any other man living within the range of notoriety, showed the singular primitive quality that belongs to ultimate matter--the quality that mediaeval theology assigned to God--he was pure act.
signatures.why: Signature fusion of theology and physics applied to a person.

signatures.passage_hint: Seneca closed the vast circle of his knowledge by learning that a friend in power was a friend lost--a fact very much worth insisting upon
signatures.why: Restates the book's recurring maxim with ironic classical scale.

signatures.passage_hint: Power is poison.
signatures.why: Bluntest formulation of a running theme.

signatures.passage_hint: Roosevelts are born and never can be taught; but Lodge was a creature of teaching--Boston incarnate--the child of his local parentage
signatures.why: Ties the Lodge portrait to the theme of education.

signatures.passage_hint: Modern politics is, at bottom, a struggle not of men but of forces.
signatures.why: Thesis linking politics to the dynamic theory.

signatures.passage_hint: Probably this was the moment of highest knowledge that a scholar could ever reach.
signatures.why: Echoes the chapter title and sets up the reversal.

signatures.passage_hint: They knew nothing themselves. Only by comparison of their ignorance could the student measure his own.
signatures.why: Characteristic closing deflation into ignorance.

signatures.passage_hint: After so many years of effort to find one's drift, the drift found the seeker
signatures.why: Characteristic chiasmus marking passivity.

signatures.passage_hint: he began to mimic Faraday's trick of seeing lines of force all about him, where he had always seen lines of will.
signatures.why: Key pivot from will to force.

signatures.passage_hint: My dear outcast, what is it you seek? This is the Church of Christ!
signatures.why: The Virgin's invented speech; its tenderness and irony are verbal.

signatures.passage_hint: We deal with Multiplicity and call it God.
signatures.why: Aquinas' imagined formula anchoring unity versus multiplicity.

signatures.passage_hint: Thought alone was Form. Mind and Unity flourished or perished together.
signatures.why: Core thirteenth-century premise later used as a measuring point.

signatures.passage_hint: Nihilism had no bottom.
signatures.why: Terse epigram in the sounding metaphor.

signatures.passage_hint: He was an acrobat, with a dwarf on his back, crossing a chasm on a slack-rope, and commonly breaking his neck.
signatures.why: Memorable image of sanity as an unstable artifice.

signatures.passage_hint: Mont-Saint-Michel and Chartres: a Study of Thirteenth-Century Unity.
signatures.why: Exact titles of the two points of relation.

signatures.passage_hint: To reduce friction is the chief use of friendship, and in politics the loss by friction is outrageous.
signatures.why: Mechanical aphorism applied to friendship.

signatures.passage_hint: What and where was the vis nova that could hold its own before this prodigious ice-cap of vis inertiae?
signatures.why: The title question; sets up the next chapter.

signatures.passage_hint: Whatever else stops, the woman must go on reproducing, as she did in the Siluria of Pteraspis; sex is a vital condition, and race only a local one.
signatures.why: Links sex-inertia to the Pteraspis motif.

signatures.passage_hint: Without an instant's hesitation, she was sure to answer: "Because the American man is a failure!" She meant it.
signatures.why: Dialogue punch line with its premise.

signatures.passage_hint: She must, like the man, marry machinery.
signatures.why: Central epigram of the woman argument.

signatures.passage_hint: whether she would rather be victim to a man, a church, or a machine.
signatures.why: Closing triad of the Marguerite passage.

signatures.passage_hint: One was almost glad to act the part of horseshoe crab in Quincy Bay
signatures.why: Self-mocking callback ending.

signatures.passage_hint: Briefly chaos is all that science can logically assert of the supersensuous.
signatures.why: Pearson's quoted claim, the chapter's hinge.

signatures.passage_hint: In plain words, Chaos was the law of nature; Order was the dream of man.
signatures.why: Adams's translation of Pearson into epigram.

signatures.passage_hint: Suddenly, in 1900, science raised its head and denied.
signatures.why: One-line paragraph; dramatic pivot.

signatures.passage_hint: when, in 1898, Mme. Curie threw on his desk the metaphysical bomb she called radium.
signatures.why: Vivid image tying science to the bomb motif.

signatures.passage_hint: to Poincare, it was a convenience; and to Karl Pearson, a medium of exchange.
signatures.why: End of the Truth genealogy; ironic climax.

signatures.passage_hint: Only in 1900, the continuity snapped.
signatures.why: Statement of the rupture.

signatures.passage_hint: The date was convenient, and convenience was truth.
signatures.why: Poincare-style irony turned on Balfour.

signatures.passage_hint: it must merge in its supersensual multiverse, or succumb to it.
signatures.why: Final alternative.

signatures.passage_hint: For once, the conspiracy of silence became crime.
signatures.why: Ironic pivot that defines Europe's silence about the coming Russo-Japanese war.

signatures.passage_hint: "I could do it myself; I could stop it to-morrow!"
signatures.why: Roosevelt's performed speech, the measuring standard of non-inert energy.

signatures.passage_hint: he was the child of steam and the brother of the dynamo
signatures.why: Key formula for the new American; it links to the dynamo symbol.

signatures.passage_hint: Apparently the Virgin--or her Son--had no longer the force to build expositions that one cared to visit, but had the force to close them.
signatures.why: Paradox joining St. Louis and Coutances as two measurements of force.

signatures.passage_hint: the conservative Christian anarchist had come to his own, but which was he--the murderer or the murdered?
signatures.why: Self-ironic climax of the Plehve scene.

signatures.passage_hint: The stupendous failure of Christianity tortured history.
signatures.why: Thesis sentence, echoed in the final chapter.

signatures.passage_hint: Among indefinite possible orbits, one sought the orbit which would best satisfy the observed movement of the runaway star Groombridge, 1838, commonly called Henry Adams.
signatures.why: Signature self-image as an astronomical body; sets up the comet imagery of later chapters.

signatures.passage_hint: to shape after his own needs the values of a Dynamic Theory of History.
signatures.why: Hand-off to the next chapter's title.

signatures.passage_hint: A DYNAMIC theory, like most theories, begins by begging the question: it defines Progress as the development and economy of Forces.
signatures.why: Self-undercutting definition that founds the theory.

signatures.passage_hint: The sum of force attracts; the feeble atom or molecule called man is attracted; he suffers education or growth; he is the sum of the forces that attract him;
signatures.why: Central inversion: nature captures man.

signatures.passage_hint: Susceptibility to the highest forces is the highest genius; selection between them is the highest science; their mass is the highest educator.
signatures.why: Aphoristic triad, the theory's ethic of education.

signatures.passage_hint: Good taste forbids saying that Constantine the Great speculated as audaciously as a modern stock-broker on values of which he knew at the utmost only the volume;
signatures.why: Signature comic-commercial reading of the Edict of Milan.

signatures.passage_hint: The laity, the people, the million, almost to a man, bet on the gods as they bet on a horse.
signatures.why: Concrete deflation of religion as fetish-power.

signatures.passage_hint: This persistence of thought-inertia is the leading idea of modern history.
signatures.why: Thesis linking the medieval and modern sections.

signatures.passage_hint: thought did not evolve nature, but nature evolved thought.
signatures.why: The Baconian reversal stated as law.

signatures.passage_hint: before which the man of science stood at first as bewildered and helpless as, in the fourth century, a priest of Isis before the Cross of Christ.
signatures.why: Analogy that ties 1900 to the year 300; it closes the historical sweep.

signatures.passage_hint: IMAGES are not arguments, rarely even lead to proof, but the mind craves them,
signatures.why: Methodological disclaimer framing everything that follows.

signatures.passage_hint: The mind, by analogy, may figure as such a comet, the better because it also defies law.
signatures.why: Governing image, picked up in the final chapter's 'perihelion.'

signatures.passage_hint: The coal-output of the world, speaking roughly, doubled every ten years between 1840 and 1900, in the form of utilized power,
signatures.why: The dynamometer measure.

signatures.passage_hint: resistance to superior mass is futile and fatal.
signatures.why: Moral law of the theory.

signatures.passage_hint: an elderly and timid single gentleman in Paris, who never drove down the Champs Elysees without expecting an accident, and commonly witnessing one;
signatures.why: Comic self-portrait that undercuts the cosmic register.

signatures.passage_hint: Perhaps even he might go back, in 1964, to sit with Gibbon on the steps of Ara Coeli.
signatures.why: Recurring motif projected into the future.

signatures.passage_hint: the new universe would know no law that could not be proved by its anti-law.
signatures.why: Culmination of the contradiction theme.

signatures.passage_hint: nothing yet proved that it would fail to react--but it would need to jump.
signatures.why: Closing turn of the argument.

signatures.passage_hint: The cylinder had exploded, and thrown great masses of stone and steam against the sky.
signatures.why: New York skyline as machinery out of control.

signatures.passage_hint: The two-thousand-years failure of Christianity roared upward from Broadway, and no Constantine the Great was in sight.
signatures.why: Echoes the Rome-of-Diocletian parallel from the previous chapters.

signatures.passage_hint: silence, next to good-temper, was the mark of sense.
signatures.why: Final stance; it chimes with the chapter's close.

signatures.passage_hint: "You must hold out for the peace negotiations," was the remonstrance. "I've not time!" he replied. "You'll need little time!" was the rejoinder. Each was correct.
signatures.why: Last exchange with Hay; its double irony depends on the exact wording.

signatures.passage_hint: it was only the quiet summons to follow--the assent to dismissal. It was time to go.
signatures.why: Emotional core of the ending.

signatures.passage_hint: and perhaps then, for the first time since man began his education among the carnivores, they would find a world that sensitive and timid natures could regard without a shudder.
signatures.why: The book's final sentence.

title: The Education of Henry Adams
